site_name: Microsoft, Roanoke River Regional Business Park, La Crosse, VA 23950

lead.notes: No non-directory page found that names a Microsoft building in the Roanoke River Regional Business Park or dates or confirms its operation. Microsoft's Southern Virginia community page names only Boydton, and the October 2025 Virginia fact sheet says only that Microsoft operates and is building datacenters in Mecklenburg, with no sites named. The vagrowth.com land-purchase article now redirects to an unrelated UK site. Only directory listings (cleanview, baxtel 'AVC09') mention the site, and they are not evidence.

site_name: Microsoft South Hill (Hillcrest campus), 210 Tunstall Rd, South Hill, VA 23070

lead.notes: The DatacenterDynamics tag page for 210 Tunstall Road and the earlier DCD permit article both return HTTP 403, so I could not read them. Microsoft's Southern Virginia community page does not mention South Hill, Hillcrest, or Tunstall Road. Directory listings disagree: one lists AVC01 as operational and AVC02/AVC03 as under construction. They are not evidence. I found no dated non-directory page on status or opening.

site_name: NTT Global Data Centers VA10 (The Grove at Gainesville campus), 14300 John Marshall Hwy, Gainesville, VA 20155

lead.notes: The Prince William Times article (July 25, 2024) describes the first of four NTT buildings at 'The Grove at Gainesville' near I-66 and US 29 as a structure still rising, so it was under construction then. The article gives no street address. NTT's own VA11 page (7251 Grove Hill Blvd) says VA11 opens in early 2027, but NTT's Northern Virginia pages do not list VA10. The March 2026 DCK article mentions Gainesville leases but gives no VA10 status. I found no page stating that VA10 opened, so the year is not bracketed. Directory listings saying 'operational' are not evidence.

site_name: Microsoft Cheyenne, Section 28 T13N R66W, about 6 miles SSE of Cheyenne, WY (probably the Bison Business Park area off S. Greeley Hwy; identity unconfirmed)

lead.notes: OpenStreetMap labels the polygon at these coordinates 'Microsoft Bison Business Park Data Center'. That is an inference aid only, not evidence. Microsoft's Nov 22, 2021 Azure blog announces a Bison Business Park datacenter that 'will be built', and Cowboy State Daily's 'launched' (Nov 2021) repeats that announcement, so neither dates an opening. A separate May 2025 DEQ proposal (WyoFile) for 128 generators at new facilities Microsoft 'plans to construct five miles southeast of Cheyenne' could also match this parcel, and I could not tell which permit this record is. HR Ranch Road geocodes about 5 miles northeast, so it is a different site. The earlier 2013 date belongs to the campus west of Cheyenne and does not apply here.
